Incorporating Beige Book insights, activity was modest in April–May with some regional softness (e.g., New York decline) even as leisure spending held up. Labor markets remained generally solid with employment increases across several districts, but signs of cooling emerged in construction, transportation, and finance, alongside weaker labor demand and some headcount reductions. Wage pressures eased and price pressures varied by district. Layered on top of broad, ongoing credit tightening from SLOOS, these Beige Book signals tilt the near-term outlook more cautious, with downside growth risks modestly outweighing positives.
